We are a firm dedicated to the personalized provision of legal services in administrative and tax matters, with a high degree of specialization.

Our vocation is customer service, seeking at all times to exceed any expectations and solve problems in a comprehensive way. We do this through experience, optimal preparation, persistence and determination that distinguish us, taking as a guiding principle of our actions the most solid ethical and moral principles.

We seek to build a long-term relationship of trust with our clients, contributing with determination in the growth and overall vision development of their projects, especially in the region of Guadalajara and throughout the State of Jalisco, where most of our clients operate. Your complete satisfaction is and will always be our goal, and our greatest triumph.

Our professional services in the region include administrative, public law and tax practice.

The team of lawyers is formed by our founding partner José Pablo Ramos Castillo, who works hand in hand with associate attorneys, Juan Carlos de Obeso Orendain , Edgar Adrián Moro López, Mónica Dariane Cárdenas Fregoso, Cecilia Cortés Diaz Corona, Hector Alejandro Sánchez Carrera, Daniel Rocha Peña and Sara Elena Vizcaino Sedano.

Most of our clients are companies with interests in different primary, secondary and tertiary economic sectors, i.e., those that carry out their activities in the energy sector, in the construction industry and in real estate services.

In many cases, we represent the interests of companies such as:


HOLCIM MÉXICO OPERACIONES, S.A. de C.V.,
INMOBILIARIA DESARROLLO LA PRIMAVERA, S.A. de C.V.
IDEX - Brasilia.
GRUPO R -CONCESIÓN ZAPOPAN.

The differentiating factor of our firm lies in the quality and high specialization we have in Amparo Proceedings and Administrative Law in general, with which we guarantee an efficient legal defense of our clients.

One of the most relevant cases that the firm handles and that concern the practice of General Business Law in Guadalajara and in the state of Jalisco is where we represented INMOBILIARIA Y DESARROLLOS LA PRIMAVERA, S.A. de C.V. in an action against the Governments of the State of Jalisco and the Municipality of Zapopan for having appropriated without prior compensation a property that belongs to our client.

Therefore, our firm was able to demonstrate, through expert evidence on real estate identification, that the State Government had unjustifiably invaded our client's private property, since such property is not located in the place or area stipulated in the Agreement.

Our firm successfully resolves conflicts involving government participation that affect our clients. On many occasions, the legal performance of our team of lawyers has achieved the establishment of jurisdictional and administrative precedents of great relevance and that guarantee the operation of many companies, contributing an incalculable value to the economic development of the region.

Another of the most relevant cases that the firm has been handling recently involves the area of energy and natural resources. In this regard, our firm represents the interests of NEXT ENERGY DE MEXICO, S.A. DE C.V. against the refusal of the Energy Regulatory Commission to grant the permit as an electric power generator for the implementation of a photovoltaic power plant with a projected installed capacity of 300.532 MW DC and an interconnection point capacity of 267.575 MW AC to supply 754,892 MWh, which would be located in the State of Baja California.

This case is highly relevant because it would not only promote the social, cultural and economic development of the region, but would also be a reflection of Mexico's true Energy Reform.

These cases are evidence of Ramos Castillo's significant professional deployment, knowledge and legal expertise throughout the Jalisco region and surrounding areas.

matters.title: Publishable Matter 1
matters.client: GRUPO R -CONCESIÓN- ZAPOPAN. GRUPO R began its operations in the area of fuel service stations and has recently expanded into the energy sector as a public lighting operator and clean energy generator for the National Electric System, making it one of the main energy companies in the State of Jalisco.
matters.rawNotes:
GRUPO R was awarded the Public Lighting Concession of Zapopan in the State of Jalisco, with an approximate value of more than 4 billion mexican pesos for a term of 18 years, after participating in a public bidding process.
Given the magnitude of the matter, the non-winning bidders and third parties filed multiple lawsuits to paralyze and revoke the concession. Approximately 35 lawsuits were filed to challenge the concession.
In these lawsuits, the plaintiffs argued that the bidding process should have been awarded to them because GRUPO R allegedly did not comply with the legal requirements set forth in the bidding conditions, or because their technical proposal (for lighting fixtures or the provision of public lighting services), as well as their economic proposal, was allegedly better than that of our client.
Thanks to our firm's legal advice, we have obtained more than 30 favourable resolutions for our client, denying lawsuits that were promoted against the awarding of the concession.
We were able to establish very important legal criteria, such as: i) that the effects of the concession and the concession contract signed cannot be paralyzed, since it has public order and social interest purposes; ii) that third parties who did not participate in the bidding process consented to the bases of the procedure, so they cannot claim issues inherent to it; and above all, iii) it was proven that the award to our client was correct, since it was the best proposal.
To date, only 3 lawsuits are still pending, the rest were favorably resolved in favor of the company, thanks to the work of the firm.
This case is highly relevant because it aims to protect a concession that has social utility, public order and social interest purposes; besides allowing the company to position itself as a regional leader in public lighting thanks to its commitment to innovation, among other elements.

matters.client: IDEX - Brasilia. Idex is an innovative company in the construction industry, leader in the State of Jalisco, with 45 years of experience in the area.
matters.rawNotes:
IDEX, among its various projects, initiated the commercially denominated "Brasilia", located in the city of Guadalajara, Jalisco, consisting of a vertical development of 328 housing units and 20 commercial units.
This development was the object of a serious attack by neighbors, neighborhood associations and the State Urban Development Attorney's Office (PRODEUR), who launched media, legal and jurisdictional attacks, alleging that "Brasilia" affected the correct urban development of the city, since it allegedly had a negative impact on traffic, concentration of inhabitants, water and electricity services and the enjoyment of the city, in addition to claiming alleged damage to groundwater.
The aforementioned, without having any real legal basis, but simply the pretension of obtaining benefits through collective pressure.
These organizations sought the closure, obstruction and non-execution of Brasilia by filing several injunction lawsuits, requesting suspensions and exerting pressure through the authorities.
As a result, the development was the victim of four simultaneous suspensions that ordered the closure of the development, based on alleged environmental impacts and risks. These suspensions were the result of four different lawsuits that ordered the closure of the project to prevent its execution.
Our team of lawyers managed to revoke the four suspensions in a period of 3 weeks, generating important legal criteria, such as: (i) the environmental impact must be sufficiently accredited as something real, actual and imminent and not only as a mere assumption without basis; (ii) although there is a Supreme Court criterion to immediately halt developments when an environmental impact is alleged, we achieved its application in a balanced manner, leaving established that whoever claims an environmental impact or risk must do so with sufficient grounds and not based on allegations without technical support.
Our firm was able to establish a very important legal precedent, even though the Supreme Court of Justice of Mexico ruled against it. As a result, developers now have guarantees regarding the continuity of their operations. This case evidenced a clear opportunity to defend against generic or unfounded allegations of environmental damage.

matters.title: Publishable Matter 3
matters.client: EL CIELO COUNTRY CLUB. (https://elcielocc.com/) A first class development located in the Bugambilias hill, where urbanity is combined with respect and coexistence with nature, making it one of the most attractive developments in the State of Jalisco.
matters.rawNotes:
The Government of the State of Jalisco and the Municipality of Tlajomulco (in the same State), issued administrative Decrees, by means of which it was determined that El Cielo Country Club represents a Natural Protected Area. As a consequence of these Decrees, the urbanisation process of said area was stopped.
The aforementioned implied a very serious impact on the property and a serious risk to the continuity and subsistence of the development, as well as to the property of the purchasers.
Against such decrees, our team of lawyers filed two amparo lawsuits, one in 2018 and the other in 2021.
In the first one, our firm achieved a very important resolution in the first instance, where it was recognized: i) the legality of the development; ii) the validity of the permits for a housing development granted prior to the Decrees that intended to disqualify the development; and above all, iii) that the development does not affect the environment, but on the contrary, it is environmentally friendly, sustainable and combines urbanisation with respect and coexistence with nature.
This criterion is of great importance, not only for the company that maintains the development, its patrimony, its image and subsistence, but also for third parties. At the legal level, the work of our firm was key to set a very important precedent.
In this way, it is established that it is not possible for political decisions to disregard land uses already granted and in execution, since the authority is obliged to respect the authorizations issued, which generates legal certainty for investment in urban development.
 This matter demonstrates that the environment is a sensitive issue and environmental measures must be technically based on scientific studies.
The Amparo filed by our firm in 2021, is in the stage of integration of expert evidence, awaiting resolution in early 2024.

matters.rawNotes:
In this case, our firm is defending the viability and continuity of one of the most ambitious real estate projects in the State of Jalisco, developed by our client and currently located in the Municipality of San Pedro Tlaquepaque.
The client came to us when the Sixth District Court in Administrative, Civil and Labor Matters in the State of Jalisco, in the framework of an amparo trial, issued the decision to suspend the aforementioned project definitively.
 The members of the Asociación Civil Cerro Guardián del Agua filed the amparo lawsuit against the licenses and authorizations granted to our client for the development of the project. The court ordered the suspension of any activity involving the movement of geological material in the Municipality of San Pedro Tlaquepaque as a result of the aforementioned amparo lawsuit.

These lawsuits are of vital importance for the company, since their favorable resolution will prevent economic, logistical and commercial damages and will guarantee the regularity and continuity of our client's business operations.

The Decree of the Regional Executive unjustifiably affects the right of use and exploitation that our client has over an area of land that corresponds to the rustic property called "Las Toronjas", in the Municipality of Leon, Guanajuato. matters.rawNotes:
On February 28, 2017, was published in the Official Gazette of the State of Jalisco the "Agreement of the Citizen Constitutional Governor of the State", ordering the administrative recovery of various properties or real estate located in the tributaries of the roads, Avenida Acueducto, Anillo Periférico and Avenida de la Patria, in the Municipality of Zapopan, of the State of Jalisco. In accordance with the Agreement, the properties are destined to a public service, and in this particular case, to the supply of drinking water to the city of Guadalajara.
This decree of administrative recovery implies that such properties become state property, of public domain and of common use. In this sense, these properties should be free of all physical barriers that restrict the access, enjoyment and use of the same, according to the terms of the Agreement.
One of the properties subject to administrative recovery belongs to our client: INMOBILIARIA DESARROLLO LA PRIMAVERA. In an unjustified manner, the possession of its property was taken away and disposed of for purposes that were not those indicated in the Administrative Agreement.
Therefore, our firm initiated a contingency plan with various legal actions, among which the amparo lawsuit 932/2017 before the Second District Court in Administrative, Civil and Labor Matters in the State of Jalisco stood out, where we were able to demonstrate, through expert evidence on real estate identification, that the properties acquired by the Government of the State of Jalisco are not located in the place or area stipulated in the Agreement and that, therefore, they had unjustifiably invaded our client's private property.
Therefore, our client acquired legal standing to request compensation for expropriation or to demand the restitution of the property.

The Group has evolved since 1928 when it originated in Switzerland and has more than 180 years of experience in the industry.
matters.rawNotes:
Due to its commercial relevance in the region, the company was the target of extortion acts undertaken by various groups in collusion with public officials of the Administrative Justice Court of the State of Jalisco. These groups sought to coerce the company into agreeing to certain economic conditions in exchange for not halting its production and marketing operations in the region.
The company did not accept the extortion and these groups initiated a nullity suit before the Sixth Unitary Chamber of the Administrative Justice Court of the State of Jalisco, from where several measures were dictated (illegal, from our point of view), whose purpose was to affect the viability of three concrete plants of the company, causing the Municipalities to ignore the permits, authorizations and operating licenses, forcing the plants to close or suspend their activities.
In order to counteract the above and lay the foundations for a fair legal defense, our firm initiated several amparo proceedings before the District Courts in Administrative, Civil and Labor Matters in the State of Jalisco, obtaining the necessary judicial suspensions and resolutions to disqualify the actions of the Sixth Unitary Chamber of the Administrative Justice Court of the State of Jalisco.
Our firm defended HOLCIM MÉXICO OPERACIONES, S.A. DE C.V. against arbitrary and illegal acts of the Sixth Unitary Chamber of the Court of Administrative Justice of the State of Jalisco, where not only were affecting the viability of three concrete plants located in the State of Jalisco, but also, and through illegal precautionary measures, the effects of the licenses or authorizations that our client has for its operation had been ignored and suspended. Evidently, the case is very relevant due to the economic and operational implications of such concrete plants.
Thanks to the defense employed by our team of lawyers HOLCIM MÉXICO OPERACIONES, S.A. DE C.V. has been able to maintain uninterruptedly its activities in the State of Jalisco.
It is important to highlight that our firm became a reference in Jalisco to defend the interests of those who are affected by absurd, disproportionate and illegal acts of the Administrative Justice Court of the State of Jalisco.

This was done to formulate the appropriate legal strategy.
An indirect amparo lawsuit was filed to challenge the constitutionality of the expropriation decree, as well as to obtain a suspension measure to halt the effects of the decree.

matters.client: DIAGEO MÉXICO OPERACIONES, SOCIEDAD ANÓNIMA DE CAPITAL VARIABLE (DIAGEO)
matters.rawNotes:
"Diageo" is an international company with over 200 brands such as "Don Julio," "Johnnie Walker," "Buchanan's," among others, and sales in nearly 180 countries. Therefore, in an effort to maintain its presence in the national territory and streamline its production and distribution network, it made an approximate investment of $1,000,000,000.00 (one billion pesos 00/100 MXN) for the implementation of an agro-industrial tequila production plant in the Municipality of La Barca, Jalisco.
However, despite "Diageo" taking special care in obtaining the necessary permits, approvals, and authorizations for the implementation of the aforementioned industrial project, it had to confront various arbitrary actions by the Municipality of La Barca, after being prevented from obtaining the renewals or extensions of the licenses that allow the urbanization processes on the properties supporting the urban development.
In light of the issues that arose and the inconveniences caused by the various closures and suspensions decreed by the municipal authorities, our firm filed nullity lawsuit 2017/2024 with the statistical index of the Sixth Unitary Chamber of the Administrative Justice Court of the State of Jalisco, where we obtained the necessary precautionary measure to ensure the continuation of construction processes and the operations that "Diageo" had been authorized to carry out by the municipal authorities.
The relevance and importance of the case stem from the type of industry and the investment our client made in the State of Jalisco. Therefore, its reopening was not a simple task due to the complications imposed by the Municipality of La Barca. It was necessary to interpret and justify the concepts of public order and social interest to obtain the precautionary measure that would allow the continuation of operations in the implementation of the agro-industrial tequila production plant.

matters.client: ROSA DORINA OCHOA GAMBOA. Individual private owner of expropriated property in Lomas del Valle.
matters.rawNotes:
The client is an individual who owns an undeveloped property in Lomas del Valle.
The parties involved are the National Water Commission, Civil Protection, the Lomas del Valle Homeowners' Association, and the property owner.
The client owns a property adjacent to a subterranean stream that is national property. Following a complaint by the homeowners' association to Conagua requesting the demarcation of the stream and its federal zone, the client's private ownership was disregarded, with an attempt to classify part of her property as national property.
This matter is relevant because it involves the deprivation of private property from an individual without a prior trial or compensation, in violation of fundamental human rights.
This amparo lawsuit involves a technical dispute, where experts and lawyers must resolve the distinction between public property and private property.
The complexity lies in determining whether the stream and its federal zone predate the private property, and whether there remains an obligation to compensate the owner.
It is a lawsuit for the expropriation of property without compensation, in violation of fundamental human rights.

matters.title: Publishable Matter 18
matters.client: SMB PROMOTORA, S.A. DE C.V. Real estate development company
matters.rawNotes:
SMB PROMOTORA, S.A. de C.V. It is a real estate development company that entered into an installment payment agreement for a contribution with the Municipality.
The parties involved are the Treasury of the Municipality of Zapopan, responsible for collecting contributions, and the client.
In this particular case, as the installment payment agreement was not fulfilled, the Municipality demanded payment through a payment order, with a warning of the seizure of all assets within a period of 6 business days. This was despite the existence of a surety bond that guaranteed the payment of the contribution
This matter is of significant relevance to the client, as it involved the seizure of all their assets for the amount of $19,476,764.61, the value of the contribution.
This amparo lawsuit required admission and the granting of a suspension to prevent the seizure of assets within the 6-business-day period. Otherwise, the seizure would result in a severe impact on the company's assets and development.
The technical complexity lay in convincing the judge to accept the case, as it involved an act not evidently admissible in an amparo lawsuit, coupled with the risk of the suspension being denied on the grounds that it could impact the public interest.
This lawsuit is included due to the successful granting of the suspension and its substantial value.

matters.title: Publishable Matter 19
matters.client: PAQUETEXPRESS is a company engaged in nationwide delivery and courier services.
matters.rawNotes:
PAQUETEXPRESS, S.A. de C.V. is a company dedicated to nationwide parcel delivery, using its own fleet of vehicles. The courier company has gasoline and diesel tanks at its disposal, which it leases to a licensed company for the commercialization of these products.
However, it has been a victim of extortion, involving federal authorities such as the Energy Regulatory Commission (CRE), ASEA, and the National Hydrocarbons Commission, who have threatened to shut down its tanks, allegedly due to a lack of required operational permits. Should this occur, it would significantly impact its logistics and, consequently, its profitability.
Therefore, a federal suspension was requested to allow the continued operation of the self-consumption tank, free from arbitrary interference.
The significance of the matter lies in the essential role of fuel as a basic input and the importance of maintaining its current logistics. This would allow the trucks to refuel at stations exclusively for Paquetexpress, S.A. de C.V., thereby streamlining operations.
The case presented a technical challenge, as the company is neither the owner of the self-consumption tanks nor the licensee to distribute the fuel. Therefore, we had to demonstrate a legitimate interest under the status of a fuel consumer.
The matter is truly significant, as it tested our ability to secure individual protection, despite the fact that other parties were more directly impacted by the granted suspension, all while preserving the commercial relationship.

matters.title: Publishable Matter 20
matters.client: CONCIENCIA AMBIENTAL DEVANGARY, A.C., it is dedicated to protecting the environment, as well as receiving environmental services without causing harm to natural assets.
matters.rawNotes:
The client is a non-profit civil association dedicated to acquiring real estate for the promotion and development of self-sustaining projects committed to the care, conservation, and restoration of ecosystems and the environment. It also focuses on the promotion and development of retreat centers, meditation, and contemplation spaces, as well as the practice, management, and provision of services for sports, leisure, and recreational activities. Additionally, the association fosters activities related to ecotourism, exploration, research, protection, conservation, and the restoration of ecosystems and the environment. It has significant presence and recognition in the State of Baja California Sur due to its role.
The parties involved are the authorities of the Municipality of La Paz, with presence solely in that municipality, and an indirect impact on the State of Baja California Sur due to its status as the capital of the federal entity.
Authorities from the Municipality of La Paz went to the property of the civil association to demarcate the land and block access to the owner, stating that it was a "federal zone" owned by the State. They intended to create a road that would allow the passage of motorized vehicles.
The presence of the authorities posed a danger to the environment, as the area is entirely pristine, free from environmental harm, and any construction would inevitably disrupt the local ecosystem. For this reason, a suspension was requested before a District Judge in the jurisdiction, seeking an order for the authorities to refrain from making any interventions on the complainant's land.
The gravity of the matter lies in the disregard for the right to private property and the obstruction of any ecological project within the area, as the construction of a road would urbanize a region that is entirely pristine.
Our firm was instrumental in designing the legal strategy to legally halt any actions by the authorities that would interfere with the client's property. We engaged in dialogue with neighboring residents and those who benefit from the environmental services of the area to raise awareness about the gravity of intervening with this protected land. We also provided ongoing counsel to the association in its discussions with the authorities, ensuring that the conflict did not escalate into further damage.
The matter was legally complex, as it required disproving the "social interest" argument used by the authorities to justify the need for the road, while also demonstrating the environmental harm caused by the planned construction. All of this unfolded in a political context, where the Municipality intended to undertake projects, and the neighbors were misinformed about the association's intentions.
It is of great significance, as amparo lawsuits in environmental matters extend to entire communities, with effects that go beyond the parties directly involved in the case. It is considered that by halting the actions of the authorities, the entire ecosystem has been protected, along with the environmental services it provides to the surrounding area.

matters.legal_understanding: The asset is El Cielo Country Club, whose urbanisation was halted after state and municipal decrees designated the area as a natural protected area. The firm filed two amparo proceedings challenging the decrees. The supplied 2024 update reports that the Sixth Collegiate Administrative Court upheld the 2018 amparo and that the judgment in the 2021 amparo was enforced in July 2024, with relief solely as to the client’s properties. This is direct Real Estate work concerning development permissions, land-use certainty and the continuity of a development.
matters.rationale: Core and hero: this is the clearest source-backed combination of a defined development, direct land-use restrictions, identified amparo work and a reported 2024 enforcement outcome. Any later narrative must preserve that the 2021 relief applied only to the client’s properties.
matters.source_quote: Regarding the 2021 amparo, a favorable ruling was obtained, nullifying the Decree updating the Local Ecological Management Program for the Municipality of Tlajomulco de Zúñiga, but solely as it pertains to the properties owned by our client. The judgment was duly enforced in July 2024.

matters.legal_understanding: The asset is the Durango Logistics and Industrial Center, comprising 207.5306 hectares. Registration of the client’s deed was refused because the properties were stated to have been expropriated under Decree CCXXXIX. The firm reviewed the underlying documents, formulated the legal strategy and filed an indirect amparo challenging the decree and seeking suspension. A definitive suspension protects the property and possession, but the constitutional hearing remains pending; the decree’s constitutionality and final ownership relief are unresolved. This is direct Real Estate work involving title, registration and expropriation.
matters.rationale: Core as a large, defined property-rights and expropriation defence with clearly reported interim relief. It must not be characterised as a final invalidation of the expropriation decree.
matters.source_quote: As a result of the above, the matter gained significant legal importance, with a favorable definitive suspension granted by a District Court, which ordered the suspension of any action that would affect the property and possession of the real estate comprising the Durango Logistics and Industrial Center, covering a total area of 207.5306 hectares.

matters.legal_understanding: The project is an agro-industrial tequila production plant in La Barca, Jalisco, for which the source reports an approximately MXN 1,000,000,000 investment. The legal problem was municipal refusal to renew or extend licences permitting urbanisation processes on the supporting properties, together with closures and suspensions. The firm filed nullity lawsuit 2017/2024 and obtained a precautionary measure allowing construction processes and authorised operations to continue. The matter is active, with no final merits outcome reported. This is direct Real Estate work concerning licences and urbanisation processes for a development.
matters.rationale: Core because it is a current, clearly described development-permits mandate with identified interim relief and an expressly named lead partner. Do not overstate the precautionary measure as a final resolution.
matters.source_quote: In light of the issues that arose and the inconveniences caused by the various closures and suspensions decreed by the municipal authorities, our firm filed nullity lawsuit 2017/2024 with the statistical index of the Sixth Unitary Chamber of the Administrative Justice Court of the State of Jalisco, where we obtained the necessary precautionary measure to ensure the continuation of construction processes and the operations that "Diageo" had been authorized to carry out by the municipal authorities.

matters.legal_understanding: The asset is the client’s property in Zapopan, affected by a 2017 state administrative-recovery agreement. The firm initiated a contingency plan including amparo 932/2017 and used real-estate-identification expert evidence to argue that the government had invaded private property outside the area stipulated in the agreement. The client reportedly obtained standing to seek compensation or restitution, but the matter is ongoing and neither remedy is reported as obtained. This is direct Real Estate work involving administrative taking, property boundaries and potential remedies.
matters.rationale: Core because it concerns an identified private property, alleged state appropriation and specific expert-evidence and amparo work. Do not convert standing to seek compensation or restitution into actual recovery.
matters.source_quote: Therefore, our client acquired legal standing to request compensation for expropriation or to demand the restitution of the property.

matters.legal_understanding: This confidential mandate concerns a property at 5056 Acueducto Avenue in Zapopan, measuring 11,283.33 m2, which the Jalisco government allegedly appropriated. The firm took over a case described as nearly lost, analysed the matrimonial regime of the family heads and filed a new amparo seeking recovery of the property or, failing that, compensation. The matter is ongoing; neither recovery nor compensation is reported as achieved. This is direct Real Estate work concerning alleged state taking and remedies for a defined property.
matters.rationale: Core because it directly concerns governmental appropriation of a defined property and a source-specific legal strategy. The requested remedies must not be described as obtained.
matters.source_quote: Due to a legal analysis that included the study of the matrimonial regime of the heads of the family, we were able to find a way to defend their rights, through a new amparo lawsuit to recover the property or, failing that, the indemnity payment.

matters.legal_understanding: This confidential mandate challenges NOM-247-SE-2021, which imposes commercial-information, advertising and contract requirements on persons offering, distributing or selling residential housing or land. The firm filed an amparo alleging that the authority exceeded its powers. The matter remains pending final judgment. The stated monetary amount is described as an estimate despite an undetermined alleged affectation, so no fixed matter value should be asserted. This is direct Real Estate work because the challenged regulation governs residential real-estate sales and related contracts.
matters.rationale: Core because it is a direct regulatory challenge concerning residential real-estate sales and contracts. Preserve the pending status and the source’s explanation that the alleged affectation is undetermined.

Currently, the lawsuit is still in process, pending only the issuance of the final judgement.

The firm intends to seek nullity of the administrative acts in order to recover the property or obtain indemnification. The matter is ongoing, and neither remedy is reported as obtained. matters.rationale: Core because it involves an identified land area, layered public transfers and a direct recovery-or-compensation strategy. Preserve the future-tense nature of the relief sought.
matters.source_quote: The firm's work in this case will focus on seeking the nullity of the administrative acts that allowed the irregular actions of the authorities, with the objective of recovering our client's property or obtaining indemnification as payment for the area of land that was unduly taken from our client.

matters.rationale: Core: this is directly relevant ongoing Real Estate work concerning the continuity of a development project and the defence of licences and authorisations challenged in an amparo. matters.legal_understanding: The matter concerns an ongoing defence of a real-estate development project in San Pedro Tlaquepaque. The final procedural effect of those arguments, and the ultimate outcome of the amparo, remain uncertain in the source.
matters.source_quote:
The members of the Asociación Civil Cerro Guardián del Agua filed the amparo lawsuit against the licenses and authorizations granted to our client for the development of the project. As a result, our client was prohibited from continuing with its construction processes.

matters.legal_understanding: The asset is land owned by an environmental civil association in La Paz. Municipal authorities allegedly demarcated the land, blocked owner access and intended to construct a road on an asserted federal zone. The firm designed a strategy to halt official action, advised in discussions with authorities and sought a suspension. The case is under review for final judgment and the suspension remains in effect. This is direct Real Estate work concerning access to, ownership of and governmental intervention on property, with environmental issues forming part of the dispute.
matters.rationale: Core as a property-access and public-authority intervention matter with current suspension relief. The source’s assertion of wider ecosystem protection should not be presented as a final adjudicated outcome.
matters.source_quote: Authorities from the Municipality of La Paz went to the property of the civil association to demarcate the land and block access to the owner, stating that it was a "federal zone" owned by the State. They intended to create a road that would allow the passage of motorized vehicles.

matters.legal_understanding: The asset is an undeveloped privately owned property in Lomas del Valle, adjacent to a subterranean stream. The dispute concerns an attempted classification of part of the client’s property as national property after a request to demarcate the stream and federal zone. The firm is handling an amparo involving technical expert issues distinguishing public from private property and potential compensation. The matter is at the evidentiary stage, with no reported decision or recovery. This is direct Real Estate work concerning title boundaries and alleged uncompensated deprivation.
matters.rationale: Core as a directly relevant property-boundary dispute that adds a private-owner perspective. It must remain framed as pending evidentiary litigation, not as an established expropriation or successful recovery.
matters.source_quote: This amparo lawsuit involves a technical dispute, where experts and lawyers must resolve the distinction between public property and private property.

matters.rationale: Core for direct Real Estate litigation concerning the ability to continue a defined 328-unit residential and 20-unit commercial development. The source documents the team’s revocation of four suspensions within three weeks. It also reports dismissal of the four lawsuits and suspensions, while separately stating that the Supreme Court of Justice of Mexico ruled against the firm. Because the source does not reconcile those statements or explain the scope, timing or effect of the Supreme Court ruling, the matter may be selected for its documented procedural work but not described as an unqualified overall victory or as establishing a definitive precedent.
matters.legal_understanding: The mandate concerns the Brasilia vertical development in Guadalajara and challenges seeking to halt its construction through four simultaneous suspensions and related injunction proceedings alleging urban-development and environmental impacts. This is direct Real Estate work because it concerns the legal ability to proceed with a specific development. The evidence supports that the firm obtained revocation of the four suspensions. It also contains a reported favourable completion outcome and a separate statement that the Supreme Court of Justice of Mexico ruled against the firm. The source does not identify the proceeding, issue, sequence or effect of that adverse ruling relative to the reported dismissal of the four lawsuits and suspensions. Public narrative must therefore distinguish the documented procedural work from the unresolved overall outcome and avoid claiming a definitive victory, full dismissal, or settled precedent without clarification.
matters.source_quote:
As a result, the development was the victim of four simultaneous suspensions that ordered the closure of the development, based on alleged environmental impacts and risks. These suspensions were the result of four different lawsuits that ordered the closure of the project to prevent its execution.
Our team of lawyers managed to revoke the four suspensions in a period of 3 weeks, generating important legal criteria, such as: (i) the environmental impact must be sufficiently accredited as something real, actual and imminent and not only as a mere assumption without basis; (ii) although there is a Supreme Court criterion to immediately halt developments when an environmental impact is alleged, we achieved its application in a balanced manner, leaving established that whoever claims an environmental impact or risk must do so with sufficient grounds and not based on allegations without technical support.
Our firm was able to establish a very important legal precedent, even though the Supreme Court of Justice of Mexico ruled against it.

matters.legal_understanding: The asset is El Cielo Country Club, whose urbanisation was halted after state and municipal decrees designated the area as a natural protected area. The firm filed two amparo proceedings challenging the decrees. The supplied 2024 update reports that the Sixth Collegiate Administrative Court upheld the 2018 amparo and that the judgment in the 2021 amparo was enforced in July 2024, with relief solely as to the client’s properties. This is direct Real Estate work concerning development permissions, land-use certainty and the continuity of a development.
matters.rationale: Core and hero: this is the clearest source-backed combination of a defined development, direct land-use restrictions, identified amparo work and a reported 2024 enforcement outcome. Any later narrative must preserve that the 2021 relief applied only to the client’s properties.
matters.source_quote: Regarding the 2021 amparo, a favorable ruling was obtained, nullifying the Decree updating the Local Ecological Management Program for the Municipality of Tlajomulco de Zúñiga, but solely as it pertains to the properties owned by our client. The judgment was duly enforced in July 2024.

matters.legal_understanding: The asset is the Durango Logistics and Industrial Center, comprising 207.5306 hectares. Registration of the client’s deed was refused because the properties were stated to have been expropriated under Decree CCXXXIX. The firm reviewed the underlying documents, formulated the legal strategy and filed an indirect amparo challenging the decree and seeking suspension. A definitive suspension protects the property and possession, but the constitutional hearing remains pending; the decree’s constitutionality and final ownership relief are unresolved. This is direct Real Estate work involving title, registration and expropriation.
matters.rationale: Core as a large, defined property-rights and expropriation defence with clearly reported interim relief. It must not be characterised as a final invalidation of the expropriation decree.
matters.source_quote: As a result of the above, the matter gained significant legal importance, with a favorable definitive suspension granted by a District Court, which ordered the suspension of any action that would affect the property and possession of the real estate comprising the Durango Logistics and Industrial Center, covering a total area of 207.5306 hectares.

matters.legal_understanding: The project is an agro-industrial tequila production plant in La Barca, Jalisco, for which the source reports an approximately MXN 1,000,000,000 investment. The legal problem was municipal refusal to renew or extend licences permitting urbanisation processes on the supporting properties, together with closures and suspensions. The firm filed nullity lawsuit 2017/2024 and obtained a precautionary measure allowing construction processes and authorised operations to continue. The matter is active, with no final merits outcome reported. This is direct Real Estate work concerning licences and urbanisation processes for a development.
matters.rationale: Core because it is a current, clearly described development-permits mandate with identified interim relief and an expressly named lead partner. Do not overstate the precautionary measure as a final resolution.
matters.source_quote: In light of the issues that arose and the inconveniences caused by the various closures and suspensions decreed by the municipal authorities, our firm filed nullity lawsuit 2017/2024 with the statistical index of the Sixth Unitary Chamber of the Administrative Justice Court of the State of Jalisco, where we obtained the necessary precautionary measure to ensure the continuation of construction processes and the operations that "Diageo" had been authorized to carry out by the municipal authorities.

matters.legal_understanding: The asset is the client’s property in Zapopan, affected by a 2017 state administrative-recovery agreement. The firm initiated a contingency plan including amparo 932/2017 and used real-estate-identification expert evidence to argue that the government had invaded private property outside the area stipulated in the agreement. The client reportedly obtained standing to seek compensation or restitution, but the matter is ongoing and neither remedy is reported as obtained. This is direct Real Estate work involving administrative taking, property boundaries and potential remedies.
matters.rationale: Core because it concerns an identified private property, alleged state appropriation and specific expert-evidence and amparo work. Do not convert standing to seek compensation or restitution into actual recovery.
matters.source_quote: Therefore, our client acquired legal standing to request compensation for expropriation or to demand the restitution of the property.

matters.legal_understanding: This confidential mandate concerns a property at 5056 Acueducto Avenue in Zapopan, measuring 11,283.33 m2, which the Jalisco government allegedly appropriated. The firm took over a case described as nearly lost, analysed the matrimonial regime of the family heads and filed a new amparo seeking recovery of the property or, failing that, compensation. The matter is ongoing; neither recovery nor compensation is reported as achieved. This is direct Real Estate work concerning alleged state taking and remedies for a defined property.
matters.rationale: Core because it directly concerns governmental appropriation of a defined property and a source-specific legal strategy. The requested remedies must not be described as obtained.
matters.source_quote: Due to a legal analysis that included the study of the matrimonial regime of the heads of the family, we were able to find a way to defend their rights, through a new amparo lawsuit to recover the property or, failing that, the indemnity payment.

matters.legal_understanding: This confidential mandate challenges NOM-247-SE-2021, which imposes commercial-information, advertising and contract requirements on persons offering, distributing or selling residential housing or land. The firm filed an amparo alleging that the authority exceeded its powers. The matter remains pending final judgment. The stated monetary amount is described as an estimate despite an undetermined alleged affectation, so no fixed matter value should be asserted. This is direct Real Estate work because the challenged regulation governs residential real-estate sales and related contracts.
matters.rationale: Core because it is a direct regulatory challenge concerning residential real-estate sales and contracts. Preserve the pending status and the source’s explanation that the alleged affectation is undetermined.
matters.source_quote: The matter involves the filing of an amparo lawsuit against the MEXICAN OFFICIAL STANDARD, not only to defend the rights of this client, but also of many other companies engaged in the construction of residential real estate, which now have the obligation to comply with excessive requirements due to a Mexican official standard. Currently, the lawsuit is still in process, pending only the issuance of the final judgement.

matters.legal_understanding: This confidential mandate concerns approximately 10 hectares owned by the client that were affected by a purported cession of rights to the Tonalá municipal government, later donated to CETI Tonalá and incorporated as national property. The firm intends to seek nullity of the administrative acts in order to recover the property or obtain indemnification. The matter is ongoing, and neither remedy is reported as obtained. This is direct Real Estate work involving a disputed governmental transfer and possible recovery or compensation for land.
matters.rationale: Core because it involves an identified land area, layered public transfers and a direct recovery-or-compensation strategy. Preserve the future-tense nature of the relief sought.
matters.source_quote: The firm's work in this case will focus on seeking the nullity of the administrative acts that allowed the irregular actions of the authorities, with the objective of recovering our client's property or obtaining indemnification as payment for the area of land that was unduly taken from our client.

matters.rationale: Core: this is directly relevant ongoing Real Estate work concerning the continuity of a development project and the defence of licences and authorisations challenged in an amparo. The submission should distinguish the challenged licences and authorisations from the court-ordered effect: suspension of activities involving movement of geological material. The source supports the firm’s reported legal work to counter the measure and its ongoing defence, but not an unqualified final result.
matters.legal_understanding: The matter concerns an ongoing defence of a real-estate development project in San Pedro Tlaquepaque. The amparo lawsuit challenged licences and authorisations granted for the project; the court’s reported suspension order was directed to activities involving movement of geological material, which prevented the client from continuing construction processes. The firm reports having advanced legal arguments intended to stop the effects and consequences of that measure and remains responsible for defending the client’s rights to continue development. The final procedural effect of those arguments, and the ultimate outcome of the amparo, remain uncertain in the source.
matters.source_quote:
The members of the Asociación Civil Cerro Guardián del Agua filed the amparo lawsuit against the licenses and authorizations granted to our client for the development of the project. The court ordered the suspension of any activity involving the movement of geological material in the Municipality of San Pedro Tlaquepaque as a result of the aforementioned amparo lawsuit.
As a result, our client was prohibited from continuing with its construction processes.

matters.legal_understanding: The asset is land owned by an environmental civil association in La Paz. Municipal authorities allegedly demarcated the land, blocked owner access and intended to construct a road on an asserted federal zone. The firm designed a strategy to halt official action, advised in discussions with authorities and sought a suspension. The case is under review for final judgment and the suspension remains in effect. This is direct Real Estate work concerning access to, ownership of and governmental intervention on property, with environmental issues forming part of the dispute.
matters.rationale: Core as a property-access and public-authority intervention matter with current suspension relief. The source’s assertion of wider ecosystem protection should not be presented as a final adjudicated outcome.
matters.source_quote: Authorities from the Municipality of La Paz went to the property of the civil association to demarcate the land and block access to the owner, stating that it was a "federal zone" owned by the State. They intended to create a road that would allow the passage of motorized vehicles.

matters.legal_understanding: The asset is an undeveloped privately owned property in Lomas del Valle, adjacent to a subterranean stream. The dispute concerns an attempted classification of part of the client’s property as national property after a request to demarcate the stream and federal zone. The firm is handling an amparo involving technical expert issues distinguishing public from private property and potential compensation. The matter is at the evidentiary stage, with no reported decision or recovery. This is direct Real Estate work concerning title boundaries and alleged uncompensated deprivation.
matters.rationale: Core as a directly relevant property-boundary dispute that adds a private-owner perspective. It must remain framed as pending evidentiary litigation, not as an established expropriation or successful recovery.
matters.source_quote: This amparo lawsuit involves a technical dispute, where experts and lawyers must resolve the distinction between public property and private property.

matters.rationale: Core for direct Real Estate litigation concerning the ability to continue a defined 328-unit residential and 20-unit commercial development. The source documents the team’s revocation of four suspensions within three weeks. It also reports dismissal of the four lawsuits and suspensions, while separately stating that the Supreme Court of Justice of Mexico ruled against the firm. Because the source does not reconcile those statements or explain the scope, timing or effect of the Supreme Court ruling, the matter may be selected for its documented procedural work but not described as an unqualified overall victory or as establishing a definitive precedent.
matters.legal_understanding: The mandate concerns the Brasilia vertical development in Guadalajara and challenges seeking to halt its construction through four simultaneous suspensions and related injunction proceedings alleging urban-development and environmental impacts. This is direct Real Estate work because it concerns the legal ability to proceed with a specific development. The evidence supports that the firm obtained revocation of the four suspensions. It also contains a reported favourable completion outcome and a separate statement that the Supreme Court of Justice of Mexico ruled against the firm. The source does not identify the proceeding, issue, sequence or effect of that adverse ruling relative to the reported dismissal of the four lawsuits and suspensions. Public narrative must therefore distinguish the documented procedural work from the unresolved overall outcome and avoid claiming a definitive victory, full dismissal, or settled precedent without clarification.
matters.source_quote:
As a result, the development was the victim of four simultaneous suspensions that ordered the closure of the development, based on alleged environmental impacts and risks. These suspensions were the result of four different lawsuits that ordered the closure of the project to prevent its execution.
Our team of lawyers managed to revoke the four suspensions in a period of 3 weeks, generating important legal criteria, such as: (i) the environmental impact must be sufficiently accredited as something real, actual and imminent and not only as a mere assumption without basis; (ii) although there is a Supreme Court criterion to immediately halt developments when an environmental impact is alleged, we achieved its application in a balanced manner, leaving established that whoever claims an environmental impact or risk must do so with sufficient grounds and not based on allegations without technical support.
Our firm was able to establish a very important legal precedent, even though the Supreme Court of Justice of Mexico ruled against it.

The firm initiated amparo proceedings against measures that allegedly caused municipalities to disregard permits, authorisations and operating licences and risked closure or suspension of the plants. The source reports judicial suspensions and resolutions enabling uninterrupted activity, but several amparo and nullity proceedings remain ongoing. The property nexus is mixed: the work concerns operational authorisations for fixed facilities rather than land rights, development approvals or a real-estate transaction.
matters.rationale: Reserve as potentially useful administrative-permits evidence, but it is less directly Real Estate-focused than the core land-use, development-continuity and property-rights mandates.

DE C.V. against arbitrary and illegal acts of the Sixth Unitary Chamber of the Court of Administrative Justice of the State of Jalisco, where not only were affecting the viability of three concrete plants located in the State of Jalisco, but also, and through illegal precautionary measures, the effects of the licenses or authorizations that our client has for its operation had been ignored and suspended.

matters.legal_understanding: This confidential mandate concerns a property owner affected by the 2019 decree designating El Bajío, Zapopan, as an environmental recovery zone, which restricted property uses and disposition. The mandate has a direct Real Estate nexus because it concerns regulatory limits on use and disposition of real estate.
matters.rationale: Reserve pending confirmation of the procedural status and scope of the asserted restitution and precedent. The source supports direct Real Estate relevance but contains a material outcome/status tension that should not be carried into portfolio prose unresolved.
matters.source_quote: The legal argumentation applied by our team of lawyers was successful, guaranteeing the restitution of our client's property right and generating a jurisdictional precedent.

matters.legal_understanding: The stated asset is the rustic property Las Toronjas, located in León, Guanajuato, over which the client holds use and exploitation rights and has housing-development projections. The firm filed a constitutional challenge to Decree 66, described as issued by the Governor of Jalisco and updating the State Program of Urban Development and Territorial Ecological Ordering, alleging that it limits the client’s rights. The matter is ongoing with no reported result. It would be direct Real Estate work concerning planning regulation and land use, but the source contains a material jurisdictional conflict: it attributes the decree to Jalisco while locating the land in Guanajuato.
matters.rationale: Reserve pending correction of the Jalisco/Guanajuato inconsistency. The mandate is potentially strong Real Estate evidence, but it should not be presented as a coherent regulatory restriction on the identified land until the issuing authority, applicable instrument or property location is confirmed.
matters.source_quote:
Our firm was hired to file a legal action to claim the unconstitutionality of Decree 66 issued on April 2, 2019, by the Governor of the State of Jalisco, through which the update of the State Program of Urban Development and Territorial Ecological Ordering was approved.

The Decree of the Regional Executive unjustifiably affects the right of use and exploitation that our client has over an area of land that corresponds to the rustic property called "Las Toronjas", in the Municipality of Leon, Guanajuato.

matters.legal_understanding: The client is a real-estate developer facing a municipal payment order and threatened seizure of all assets due to an alleged breach of an instalment agreement for a contribution. The firm obtained admission and a suspension to prevent seizure within six business days. The legal issue is collection and asset-protection procedure rather than a defined real-estate right, development approval or property transaction; the stated status is admission.

candidates.submission_bio:
José Pablo Ramos Castillo is the founding partner of Ramos Castillo Abogados and leads the firm’s real estate administrative and constitutional litigation. He has acted for developers and property owners in disputes concerning land-use restrictions, development permissions, expropriation measures and the protection of private property.

He led the representation of El Cielo Country Club in two amparo proceedings challenging decrees that halted urbanisation of the development after it was designated as a natural protected area. The Sixth Collegiate Administrative Court of the Third Circuit upheld the amparo granted in the 2018 proceeding, while relief obtained in the 2021 proceeding nullified the update to the Local Ecological Management Programme as it applied to the client’s properties; that judgment was enforced in July 2024.

His current work includes leading the indirect amparo brought for Duranpark in connection with the expropriation decree affecting the 207.5306-hectare Durango Logistics and Industrial Center, where a definitive suspension protects the property and possession pending the constitutional hearing. He also leads mandates involving alleged governmental takings of private property, challenges to restrictions on residential real estate activity under NOM-247-SE-2021, and technical property-boundary disputes involving private land and asserted public zones.

Ramos Castillo Abogados represented El Cielo Country Club in two amparo proceedings challenging state and municipal decrees that designated the area of the development as a natural protected area and halted its urbanisation. The measures placed the continuity of the development and the position of its purchasers at risk.

The firm obtained relief in the 2018 amparo, subsequently upheld by the Sixth Collegiate Administrative Court of the Third Circuit. In the 2021 proceeding, it obtained a judgment nullifying the update to the Local Ecological Management Programme for Tlajomulco de Zúñiga insofar as it concerned the client’s properties; the judgment was enforced in July 2024. José Pablo Ramos Castillo led the matter, supported by Daniel Rocha Peña and Héctor Alejandro Sánchez Carrera. The development is valued at MXN 3.000.000.000,00.
decisive_source_quotes: José Pablo Ramos Castillo

The Government of the State of Jalisco and the Municipality of Tlajomulco (in the same State), issued administrative Decrees, by means of which it was determined that El Cielo Country Club represents a Natural Protected Area. As a consequence of these Decrees, the urbanisation process of said area was stopped.

In continuation of this matter, for the amparo filed in 2018, the Sixth Collegiate Administrative Court of the Third Circuit, under case file 347/2022, issued a ruling that upheld the amparo granted by the Court of First Instance.

Regarding the 2021 amparo, a favorable ruling was obtained, nullifying the Decree updating the Local Ecological Management Program for the Municipality of Tlajomulco de Zúñiga, but solely as it pertains to the properties owned by our client. The judgment was duly enforced in July 2024.

Ramos Castillo Abogados acted for IDEX in relation to Brasilia, a Guadalajara vertical development comprising 328 housing units and 20 commercial units. Neighbours, neighbourhood associations and PRODEUR pursued proceedings and four simultaneous suspensions that ordered closure of the project on asserted environmental-impact and risk grounds.

The firm obtained revocation of the four suspensions within three weeks, advancing arguments that environmental impact must be supported by real, current and imminent evidence rather than unsupported allegations. José Pablo Ramos Castillo led the mandate, supported by Daniel Peña Rocha and Hector Alejandro Sanchez Carrera. The development is valued at MXN 1.300.000.000,00.
decisive_source_quotes: José Pablo Ramos Castillo

IDEX, among its various projects, initiated the commercially denominated "Brasilia", located in the city of Guadalajara, Jalisco, consisting of a vertical development of 328 housing units and 20 commercial units.

As a result, the development was the victim of four simultaneous suspensions that ordered the closure of the development, based on alleged environmental impacts and risks. These suspensions were the result of four different lawsuits that ordered the closure of the project to prevent its execution.

Our team of lawyers managed to revoke the four suspensions in a period of 3 weeks, generating important legal criteria, such as: (i) the environmental impact must be sufficiently accredited as something real, actual and imminent and not only as a mere assumption without basis; (ii) although there is a Supreme Court criterion to immediately halt developments when an environmental impact is alleged, we achieved its application in a balanced manner, leaving established that whoever claims an environmental impact or risk must do so with sufficient grounds and not based on allegations without technical support.
Our firm was able to establish a very important legal precedent, even though the Supreme Court of Justice of Mexico ruled against it.
